summary: Dedicated pool throughput wobble from cross-tenant short-stream fanout causing autoscaler stalls and transient GPU shortage
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LuminaSearch reported repeated mid-day degradation on their dedicated reservation: p50 holds but p95/p99 spiked and throughput dropped by ~30% for 15-40 minute windows. Symptoms include 429s for short burst routes, GPU attach latency rising, and autoscaler failing to expand quickly (attach backoff). Impact is user-facing search latency regression for their production traffic.

Impact:
- LuminaSearch search queries see degraded throughput and elevated p99 latency during bursts (~30% throughput reduction).
- Some requests hit transient 429s / attach-timeouts and fall back to lower-capacity routes.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (LuminaSearch reservation) in prod us-west-2.
- Models: open-llama-7b pinned for a subset of routes, opt-1.3 used for lower-cost fallbacks.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic short-stream fanout spikes (many small concurrent short requests) appear to cause slot fragmentation and allocator contention.
- Autoscaler telemetry shows delayed scale-up events and repeated backoffs due to short-lived slot reservations.
- GPU attach latency increases followed by temporary shortages; allocator reports "insufficient free slots" despite overall pool capacity not fully exhausted.

Expected behavior:
- Dedicated reservation maintains predictable throughput; autoscaler should scale or reassign quickly without long attach backoffs.

Immediate customer expectations:
- Identify root cause and provide a short-term mitigation (either config/workaround or operational routing change).
- ETA for fix or operational change and communication cadence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay customer production short-stream traffic pattern in staging (high fanout of 50-200 short requests across pinned model routes).
2) Observe allocator slot distribution and GPU attach latency while toggling connection keepalive and small-batch settings.
3) Toggle autoscaler cooldown thresholds to simulate production config and measure scale-up delay under repeated short-lived slot reservations.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: short-lived connection fanout from customer SDK caused allocator fragmentation and repeated ephemeral reservations, confusing autoscaler heuristics (short lived signals not considered sustained).
Checked pool utilization: aggregate GPU memory/compute not saturated; however slot-level fragmentation observed with many small open sessions holding lightweight leases.

Telemetry gap: autoscaler uses 1m rolling metrics; short spikes of 20-40s do not always trigger scale decisions, leading to attach queueing. Consider shorter aggregation window or separate short-stream metric.
Observed correlation between high keepalive churn from customer sidecar and increase in attach latency. Logged evidence points to sidecar connection churn (see Slack #support thread).

Reproduced a partial scenario in a repro cluster by replaying short-stream pattern: allocator started serializing slot allocations, causing a queue at the attach stage even though total free slots existed.
comments: Aisha Nadar (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer first reported at 14:45 PT. They see intermittent 429s and longer tails. Requested priority escalate.
Tomas Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-12: Spun up repro cluster and replayed traffic. Confirming short-stream fanout reproduces attach queueing. Suspect allocator fairness + autoscaler window mismatch.
Eli Chen (Platform) 2026-03-13: Added additional telemetry probes to autoscaler to capture short-lived reservation signals. Opening PR to add a short-stream metric flag for dedicated pools.
LuminaSearch Ops (customer) 2026-03-13: We can change SDK keepalive from 2s to 10s for a canary if that helps; want to avoid degradations during business hours.
Tomas Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-14: Temporary mitigation pushed: enable per-tenant short-stream smoothing and increase attach worker concurrency for LuminaSearch in us-west-2. Monitoring results now.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-14): enabled short-stream smoothing and bumped attach concurrency for the affected reservation. Early telemetry shows p99 latency improving and attach queue drained.

Follow-ups: 1) Autoscaler heuristic change to include a short_stream_counter (proposal in PR #191). 2) Recommend customer SDK keepalive tuning and batching best-practice doc. 3) Operational runbook entry to detect slot-fragmentation signatures.
Customer communication: Provided LuminaSearch with summary, recommended SDK change (optional), and status check windows. Scheduling postmortem if recurrence observed.
